summary: ACCEPT. The project's first SQL-executed-against-a-real-database test, and it does the job it was commissioned for. Every scope item was verified BY EXECUTION against a real PostgreSQL 16.4 (Docker unavailable, so the reviewer built a cluster from portable binaries and ran alembic upgrade head). S1: the tests load both modules from their real paths via importlib and read module.SQL - no copy, no rewrite on the main path; the leak tests rewrite SQL only through an explicit sql= override, and _replace_once asserts the anchor is SINGULAR so a source edit cannot silently no-op a mutation. S2: the differing assertion is a literal 'assert live != empty' on top of the per-leg assertions, leg selection is plain arithmetic on the two window constants and NOT derived from the thing under test, and both legs use IDENTICAL seed rows so only the window differs - no fixture trap. Mutation-verified: patching execute() to ignore case.window and hard-code the live window turns BOTH differential tests RED. S4: no pytest.skip/skipif/xfail/importorskip anywhere in the new files or conftest; the only except re-raises. Executed four ways - DSN unset, DSN at a dead port, DSN pointing at sqlite, and psql absent from PATH - ZERO skips, exit 1 in all four, and there is no env var or marker that can turn the DB tests off. CI wiring is sound: postgres:16 service with a pg_isready health check, alembic run against it, the DSN exported on the step that runs tests/integration, no continue-on-error, no marker filter, no path exclusion; and I confirmed both check runs are on the EXACT head be6ee40f5, not a base or merge commit. ⭐⭐ THE RESULT THAT MATTERS: the three known #828 leaks die, AND three NOVEL spellings the author could not have anticipated die too - a tautological predicate on target_buy_legs, the same on target_exit_episodes, and an unbounded union inserted EARLIER in the rows CTE - each killed by a row-count assertion at RUNTIME rather than by a string anchor. This is a genuine runtime property check, so the six-round 'fix the named leak, a one-token variation survives' cycle is broken for these CTEs. ⛔ REQUIRED FOR THE README, because the green is NARROWER than it looks: 3 of D6's 5 target_* CTEs (target_refused, target_mirror_symbols, target_matched_orders) and ALL of identity's order_rows read populations that are EMPTY in the seed - no broker_order_events and no broker_orders are seeded. They are UNEXERCISED, not passing. Proven: deleting the window predicate from target_refused leaves the suite at 6 passed, and replacing order_rows' three window predicates with 1970-2999 leaves the identity test green. Say so in tests/integration/README.md so the next reader does not inherit a wider green than exists. FOLLOW-UPS, none blocking: (a) seed broker_order_events so the refused_exits NUMERATOR is windowed - the #828 harm was the denominator and that half IS guarded, this is the other direction; (b) seed broker_orders so identity's order_rows, the half carrying the actual acceptance signal, is proven; (c) add BOUNDARY rows at exactly since_at (must be included) and exactly until_at (must be excluded) - today '<' to '<=' survives on both modules, so the half-open contract is unproven, though a plus-or-minus one day widening IS caught so the outside row is not uselessly far; (d) _d6_refusal_observation discards the SQL's real CONTROL_* rows and substitutes fabricated ones to get past validate_controls, so a break in the base_* control CTEs stays green here; (e) Windows-only, pass encoding='utf-8' to the psql subprocess - the ambient cp1252 locale breaks on a non-ASCII byte in the D6 SQL. REUSABILITY is real: 121 shared lines, ~61 for the second customer, and nothing special-cases D6. Two of the remaining scripts fit with zero harness change; field_acceptance has no module-level SQL and would need an sql_attr field or an alias, and _RESET_TABLES is a shared mutable list so a third customer's addition changes reset semantics for the first two. NOTE: the harness rebuilds the psql command rather than calling module.query_database, so the module's OWN invocation shape is not proven here - the -f - versus -c shape stays pinned by the existing unit tests.
